title: Snapshot Set with Historical Reads
prompt:
Implement `SnapshotSet`, an in-memory set with versioned reads.

- `add(value) -> bool` inserts a hashable value into the current version and returns whether it changed the set.
- `remove(value) -> bool` removes a value from the current version and returns whether it changed the set.
- `snapshot() -> int` returns an immutable handle for the current version.
- `values_at(snapshot_id) -> set` returns an independent copy of the values visible at that snapshot.

Every mutating call creates a new current version, including a no-op add or remove. Snapshot IDs are zero-based and must remain valid after later mutations. Reject an unhashable value with an error; raise an error for an invalid snapshot ID. Do not expose an internal mutable set.

Invalid inputs may be rejected with `assert`.

example.input: s = SnapshotSet(); s.add('a'); before = s.snapshot(); s.add('b')
example.reasoning: Later mutations create a new version instead of changing an existing snapshot.
